text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Norwegian oil and energy minister Grete Faremo resigns in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance of a prominent left-wing politician, Berge Furre. Also, Hans Olav Oestgaard, head of the intelligence service, steps down for his role in the scandal.

- Russian authorities are denying Norwegian authorities access to data for measuring radioactivity. Instruments worth 300,000 crowns were donated by the Norwegian Foreign Ministry to Russian authorities in Polyarnye Sori, seven kilometers from the atomic power plant in Kola, a year ago.
- The wolf is the only mammal threatened with extinction in Norway.
- Oekokrim, the police economic crime squad, is being criticised by a lawyer for threatening the legal rights of those under investigation by being too ambitious in its probes.
- Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland says he will appoint a new Energy Minister by Friday.
